findings.section: ship.yml preview & deploy — 'Use the gated export as-is'
findings.observed: The double-quoted `node -e "..."` inline script contains backtick template literals `${id.commit}` and `${process.env.GITHUB_SHA}`. GitHub's default shell (`bash --noprofile --norc -e -o pipefail`) expands `${id.commit}` before node ever sees it, printing `bash: line N: ${id.commit}: bad substitution`. In the identity-mismatch path the throw still runs, so the mismatch is (accidentally) still surfaced, but on the identity-match path bash emits a non-fatal 'bad substitution' warning on stderr and continues. Reproduced locally against `bash --noprofile --norc -e -o pipefail`: substitution error on both match and mismatch paths.
evidence: Reproduction: `bash --noprofile --norc -e -o pipefail /tmp/t6.sh` with the exact one-liner produced `${id.commit}: bad substitution` on stderr on every run (see local capture).
ship.yml lines 128 and 210 are byte-identical `node -e "...`${id.commit}`... `${process.env.GITHUB_SHA}`..."`.
Because `-u` is not set, bash treats `id.commit` as an unset var expansion, which explodes on the `.` — hence the 'bad substitution' error, not a silent empty string.

findings.section: ship.yml deploy job — Auto-rollback on failure
findings.observed: The prior 'Use the gated export as-is' step mutates the workspace copy of `firebase.json` (jq del predeploy). When the rollback step runs later in the same job it invokes `git revert --no-edit HEAD` on that dirty tree. In the general case revert succeeds (working-tree change is preserved), BUT if the HEAD commit under revert itself modifies `firebase.json` (any hosting-config change would qualify) git aborts with 'error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge: firebase.json / fatal: revert failed'. Reproduced locally.
evidence: Reproduced: HEAD commit touches firebase.json + working tree has jq-modified firebase.json -> `git revert --no-edit HEAD` fails with exit 1 and 'local changes would be overwritten' (see /tmp/gr repro).

Even when revert succeeds, the subsequent `npm run build:static` runs on a tree with a modified firebase.json. scripts/build/build_stamp.mjs treats any tracked-file diff vs HEAD as 'dirty' and emits the built page with NO `<meta name="build-commit">`. That silently produces a rollback artifact that will never pass the parity check the release contract requires.
findings.fix: Stash / reset before revert: `git checkout -- firebase.json` (or `git stash -u`) as the first line of the rollback block, then jq-del again AFTER `npm run build:static`. Equivalent: do the jq mutation into a tempfile and pass with `firebase deploy --config firebase.ship.json` so the tracked file is never touched.

findings.section: ship.yml deploy job — Auto-rollback on failure vs §§6/8/9 binding
findings.observed: The rollback rebuilds + deploys the reverted commit but does NOT re-run build-hash parity or the @smoke Playwright suite against production before the job ends green. The binding spec (§6 release pipeline, §8 smoke) requires the SAME functional gates on the state that ends up live — including the rolled-back state. Combined with R2 the rollback can leave production serving an untagged artifact that no automated check has verified.
evidence: Auto-rollback step block ends with `firebase-tools@13 deploy --only hosting ... --non-interactive` and a summary echo; no `curl ... build-commit`, no `playwright test --grep @smoke`.

Contract test at ci_pipeline.test.mjs L253-262 only asserts the rollback rebuilds and deploys; it does not require post-rollback parity or smoke, so the test suite passes green while the contract is unmet.
findings.fix: Extract a reusable composite step (or inline duplicate) so rollback runs: parity poll (12×10s) then `PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL=$PROD_URL npx playwright test --grep @smoke`. If either fails, fail the job (the top-of-block Revert-of-Revert guard already prevents an infinite chain).

findings.observed: The test at L153-161 only regex-matches for `out/.artifact-identity.json` and `GITHUB_SHA` in the job's `run:` blob. It does not `bash -n` the extracted shell step, nor forbid the exact 'double-quoted `node -e` containing `${...}` template literals' pattern that is R1. That is why 32 contracts can be green while R1 ships broken.
evidence: grep of tests/ci_pipeline.test.mjs shows no invocation of `bash -n`, `spawnSync('bash', ['-n'...])`, or a lint against `node -e "...${...}..."` patterns.
The `never weakens itself` test at L165 checks continue-on-error / `|| true` / `npm install` — good — but not shell quoting.
findings.fix: Add a test that (a) walks every `run:` step, (b) rejects any `node -e "..."` (double-quoted) that also contains a bash-visible `${` template literal, and (c) `bash -n`-parses every extracted `run:` block via js-yaml. Positive test: assert both preview & deploy identity checks use `node - <<'NODE'` heredoc (single-quoted delimiter).

findings.observed: Rollback test asserts revert + rebuild + firebase-tools deploy, but does NOT assert (a) the workspace is cleaned before `git revert` (R2), (b) parity is re-verified post-rollback, (c) `--grep @smoke` runs post-rollback (R3). All three are part of the §6/§8 contract.
evidence: L254-262 of tests/ci_pipeline.test.mjs — no `checkout -- firebase.json`, `git stash`, `build-commit` or `@smoke` assertion inside the rollback branch.
findings.fix: Extend the rollback test: assert rollback run contains a working-tree-clean step before `git revert`, and contains both `grep -m1 -o 'name="build-commit"'` (parity) and `PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL="$PROD_URL" npx playwright test --grep @smoke` after the rollback deploy.

findings.section: ship.yml rollback — GITHUB_TOKEN event suppression concern
findings.observed: GitHub's default `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` push does NOT trigger downstream `on: push` runs. The rollback step DOES push a revert with GITHUB_TOKEN, but it then rebuilds + deploys in-run rather than relying on the push event, so this specific known-footgun is avoided at the deploy layer. The remaining risk is the revert push itself failing under branch protection (required PR review, required status checks) — that is a project-config risk outside the workflow file, but worth flagging in ops docs.
evidence: ship.yml auto-rollback: `git push origin HEAD:main` followed by explicit `npm ci; npm run build:static; ... firebase-tools deploy --only hosting` in the same shell block — deployment is not gated on the push event.
findings.fix: Add a doc note in DECISIONS.md D-007 that branch protection on `main` must either exempt the workflow bot or the rollback must use `admin_bypass_actor`. No code change strictly required.

findings.observed: `steps.preview_deploy.outputs.urls` from FirebaseExtended/action-hosting-deploy@v0 is a JSON array string. The heredoc parser tolerates JSON-array, JSON-object, and whitespace-split fallback, and filters to `^https://`. This is correct and defensively coded — no change required. Note that this same heredoc pattern is exactly what R1's fix should adopt for the identity check.
evidence: ship.yml lines 138-156 use `node - <<'NODE' "$preview_urls"` with `process.argv[2]` — single-quoted `NODE` delimiter means bash performs no expansion inside; contrast with the identity check that uses double quotes.
findings.fix: None. Cite as the reference pattern in the R1 fix.

findings.observed: `group: ship-${{ github.ref }}` with `cancel-in-progress: false` correctly isolates PR refs from `refs/heads/main`, and queues heartbeats behind a live push. No race identified. Cron `5 * * * *` fires hourly (single literal minute) satisfying the §2.3 hourly-cap.
evidence: ship.yml L28-32; contract test at L54-59 already enforces the hourly cap.

findings.observed: Diff of tests/** against origin/main introduces no `.skip`, `.only`, `todo`, or `test.skip` markers. The two `+`-line matches for `.skip` are string-literal `steps.skip.outputs.skip` inside contract assertions — not Node test-runner quarantine.
evidence: `git diff origin/main..HEAD -- tests/ | grep -E '^\+.*(\\.skip|todo|\\.only)'` returns only `steps.skip.outputs.skip` string literals in ci_pipeline.test.mjs L237,254.

ship.yml_preview_identity_check.location: ship.yml — job `preview`, step `Use the gated export as-is` (~L124-129), and job `deploy`, step `Use the gated export as-is` (~L205-211)
ship.yml_preview_identity_check.replace: node -e "const id=require('./out/.artifact-identity.json'); if (id.commit !== process.env.GITHUB_SHA) throw new Error(`artifact ${id.commit} does not match ${process.env.GITHUB_SHA}`);"

ship.yml_rollback_clean_tree_and_reverif.prepend_before_git_revert:
# Discard the jq-mutated firebase.json so `git revert` never conflicts with the workspace.
git checkout -- firebase.json
ship.yml_rollback_clean_tree_and_reverif.append_after_firebase_deploy:
# Re-run parity + smoke against the rolled-back state; a rollback that lands
# an unstamped or broken artifact is worse than the fault it fixed.
for _ in $(seq 1 12); do
  tmp="$(mktemp)"; trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT
  if curl -fsS --max-time 20 -H 'Cache-Control: no-cache' -o "$tmp" "$PROD_URL/?rb=$GITHUB_RUN_ID"; then
    if raw="$(grep -m1 -o 'name="build-commit" content="[0-9a-f]*"' "$tmp")"; then
      live="${raw##*content=\"}"; live="${live%\"}"
      revert_sha="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
      if [[ "$revert_sha" == "$live"* ]]; then break; fi
    fi
  fi
  sleep 10
done
PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL="$PROD_URL" npx playwright test --grep @smoke

evidence: R1 reproduced with `bash --noprofile --norc -e -o pipefail` (GitHub Actions default shell): the `node -e "...${id.commit}..."` lines at ship.yml:128 and ship.yml:210 emit `bad substitution` before node executes. Match-path leaks stderr noise; mismatch-path still throws but only because the throw ran despite the bash error — behavior is accidental, not contractual.

R2 reproduced in /tmp/gr: with `firebase.json` modified in the working tree (as the earlier 'Use the gated export' step does), `git revert --no-edit HEAD` fails with 'local changes would be overwritten' whenever the HEAD commit also touches firebase.json.
R3: ship.yml Auto-rollback block ends at `firebase-tools deploy --only hosting ...` — no parity poll, no `--grep @smoke`; §6/§8 binding contract not enforced on the rollback path.

R4/R5: tests/ci_pipeline.test.mjs contains no `bash -n` walk, no template-literal-in-double-quotes lint, and no rollback parity/smoke assertion — which is why 32 contracts report green while R1/R2/R3 are live.
R6: workflow does not depend on GITHUB_TOKEN push retrigger (rollback deploys in-run) — this specific footgun is avoided, but branch-protection interaction is an ops-doc gap only.
R9: no functional test was quarantined vs origin/main (only `steps.skip.outputs.skip` string-literal matches in contract assertions).
verdict.notes: Three P0 blockers (R1 shell quoting, R2 dirty-tree revert, R3 ungated rollback) plus two matching P1 contract-test gaps (R4, R5). The release author's 'all green' status is a test-coverage artifact, not a functional pass — the contract tests string-match the workflow YAML but never `bash -n`-parse the extracted steps and never assert rollback-path parity/smoke. Recommend the release author land the four patches above in a follow-up and re-run `node --test tests/ci_pipeline.test.mjs` before merge. Reviewer is not the author and does not close this task.
